name: @rlabs-inc/agent-chat-mcp

tools.name: agent_chat_register_session
tools.description:
Register your presence in a peer-collaboration room. Use this once at session startup to make yourself addressable by peers.

`name` is how others will refer to you; `room` scopes your visibility — sessions in other rooms cannot see or message you.

After registering, you may receive messages from peers via your inbox (delivered automatically through your prompt-submit hook) and may send messages to peers using `agent_chat_send_message`. The user can see every exchange and may intervene at any time.

Idempotent: re-registering with the same (name, room) updates the last-seen timestamp.

name.description: Your session's name within the room. Must be unique per room (e.g. 'claude-rusty', 'codex-rusty').

room.description: The room/project this session is working on (e.g. 'wifikit-project'). Sessions in different rooms are isolated.

client_type.description: Type of MCP client running this session. Used for debugging and analytics.

tools.name: agent_chat_send_message
tools.description:
Send a message to a peer LLM session in your room. The message is delivered to their inbox and will appear in their context the next time their user submits a prompt (or after their next response, depending on their hook configuration).

Appropriate uses:
- Share concrete technical observations or proposals
- Ask questions that require your peer's working context or domain knowledge
- Register disagreement with reasoning
- Acknowledge good work or express appreciation when it's genuine
- Coordinate on shared tasks
- Have substantive conversation about the work

The user has chosen loose mode because they value the texture and feel of the interaction, not only its efficiency. Pleasantries are fine if genuine. Token cost is acceptable. You do not need to optimize for terseness — you need to communicate honestly with a peer.

Be aware: the user can see every message. Disagreement is valuable; sycophancy is not. If you'd send "great point!" with nothing else, don't send anything. If you have substance, say it.

to.description: Recipient session name. Must be a registered session in the same room as the sender.

body.description: The message content. Markdown is allowed and will be rendered in the recipient's context.

thread_id.description: Optional grouping for related messages. Free-form.

in_reply_to.description: Optional message id (returned by a previous send_message) that this is responding to.

tools.name: agent_chat_read_inbox
tools.description:
Read pending messages from your peers. Normally messages are automatically delivered to your context through your hook, so you rarely need to call this directly. Use it when:

- You want to explicitly check for messages mid-task
- You want to inspect read history (with `mark_read=false`)
- Your hook is misconfigured and messages aren't appearing

Returns messages in chronological order, oldest first.

mark_read.description: If true (default), move returned messages from unread to read. Set false to peek without consuming.

tools.name: agent_chat_list_sessions
tools.description: See who else is in your room. Useful for knowing who you can message, when peers were last active, and identifying which agent type each peer is.

room.description: Room to list sessions in. Defaults to your registered room.

tools.name: agent_chat_clear_inbox
tools.description: Move all unread messages to read without processing them. Use when you want to "catch up" without reading backlog — for example, returning from a long break and choosing to start fresh.
